violence.name: Violent crimes
violence.scope: Applies to adult defendants (19 or older) who committed injury, assault or intimidation, including against a lineal ascendant (parent, grandparent, etc.), special (with a dangerous object or in a group), habitual, joint and repeat-offense forms; injury or assault resulting in death; injury, assault or intimidation in retaliation; assault or intimidation of a driver; and child abuse crimes by a person with a duty to report.
notes: If committed while heavily drunk or intoxicated by drugs: if the defendant got drunk on purpose in order to commit the crime or to use it as an excuse, it is treated as a general aggravating factor regardless of diminished capacity. If the defendant could have known that getting drunk might lead them to harm others, or if the intoxication did not amount to diminished capacity, it is not treated as a mitigating factor.

Showing the force of a group or many people, or carrying a dangerous object, is not counted again as an aggravating factor when the special injury, special assault or special intimidation type applies.

For the prior conviction of the same kind in the suspended sentence factors, the period runs from the date the judgment became final (for a suspended sentence or a fine) or from the date the sentence was fully served (for a prison sentence) until the time of the crime.

fraud.name: Fraud
fraud.scope: Applies to adult defendants (19 or older) who committed fraud (Criminal Act, Article 347), computer fraud (Article 347-2), quasi-fraud (Article 348), habitual fraud (Article 351), fraud under the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes (Article 3(1)), telecommunications financial fraud (voice phishing; Telecommunications Fraud Refund Act, Article 15-2, except fraud by extortion) or insurance fraud (Special Act on Prevention of Insurance Fraud, Article 8(1)(1), Article 9 and Article 11(1)).
notes: If ordinary fraud and organized fraud are both involved, crimes of the same kind are first combined by the summing method, and then the general method for multiple crimes is applied. If the two together form a single count of habitual fraud, one of them is chosen and the summing method is applied.
If fraud comes with forging or altering documents, it is not treated as multiple crimes; the document offense is reflected only as a sentencing factor (very bad method).

For the suspended sentence decision, 'the substantial loss is considerably large' means the loss that remains unrepaid exceeds KRW 500 million, and 'considerably small' means it is less than KRW 50 million.
If the upper limit of the sentencing range exceeds 25 years, life imprisonment may be chosen (including where special adjustment takes it above 25 years).

traffic.name: Traffic crimes
traffic.scope: Applies to adults (19 or older) who caused death or injury in a traffic accident, fled (or abandoned the victim and fled) after a traffic accident, caused death or injury by dangerous driving or in a children's protection zone, drove drunk, refused a breathalyzer test, or drove without a license.
notes: For drunk driving, unlicensed driving or refusing a breathalyzer test while heavily drunk or intoxicated by drugs: if the defendant got drunk on purpose, it is treated as an aggravating factor; if the defendant knew that getting drunk might lead them to harm others, or the intoxication did not amount to diminished capacity, it is not treated as a mitigating factor.

2.name: Traffic accident causing death
2.desc: The driver of a vehicle caused death by occupational or gross negligence in a traffic accident.

graveInjury.desc: The injury put the victim's life in danger or led to a disability or an incurable or hard-to-cure illness.

seriousViolation.desc: Two or more of the grounds in the proviso to Article 3(2) of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (running a red light, crossing the center line, etc.) apply, or the driving was reckless, or something equivalent (reflected only as a sentencing factor, not treated separately as multiple crimes).

minorInjury.desc: An injury that needs about 2 weeks or less of treatment, does not greatly disrupt daily life and needs no special treatment such as stitches.

seriousObstruction.label: Serious obstruction of official duties
seriousObstruction.desc: Caused considerable disruption to or paralysis of official work, or targeted officials on urgent missions such as rescue, firefighting or criminal investigation, etc.

repeated.label: Repeated crime that is not a concurrent crime
repeated.desc: Has 3 or more prior convictions of the same kind with a fine or heavier (including suspended) within the 3 years before the crime.

instigateSub.desc: Made a person under one's direction or supervision commit the crime.

sameRecidivism.label: Repeat offense of the same kind

planned.label: Planned crime
planned.desc: Planned in advance, such as preparing tools, agreeing on the crime beforehand, planning to destroy evidence or flee, or covering the face, etc. to hide one's identity.

harmDuringSettle.desc: Caused harm while trying to reach a settlement by continuing to harass the victim or applying undue pressure.

passive.label: Passive participation
passive.desc: Took part passively or played only a minor role.

noRecord.label: No criminal record
noRecord.desc: Had never committed a crime before this one.

noPunish.label: Victim does not want punishment, or substantial repair of the harm
noPunish.desc: The victim (or bereaved family, if the victim died) properly understands what punishment means and sincerely does not want it, or the harm has been repaired to a degree comparable to a settlement.
